content:
The test image shows a mango leaf with several dark, irregular spots. Some spots appear to be coalescing, and there might be some drying or necrosis in the center of the larger spots.

Now, I will read the `part_index.md` file to narrow down the possible classes based on the affected plant part, which is clearly a leaf.

The `part_index.md` confirms that all four possible classes (Anthracnose, Die_Back, Powdery_Mildew, Sooty_Mould) can affect the leaf. This doesn't narrow the candidates, so I will now proceed to view reference images, one from each of the top candidates.

I'll start with one reference image for each class: Anthracnose, Die_Back, Powdery_Mildew, and Sooty_Mould.

First, Anthracnose: `CyberVisionAg/Prepared_Dataset/Mango_Leaf/Anthracnose/leaf/Mango_Leaf_14.jpg`

It seems I made a mistake in the file path. I need to remove the duplicate `CyberVisionAg` from the path. I will try again with the correct path.

First, Anthracnose: `CyberVisionAg/Prepared_Dataset/Mango_Leaf/Anthracnose/leaf/Mango_Leaf_14.jpg`

This reference image for Anthracnose shows a reddish-brown leaf with significant damage and holes. This doesn't quite match the dark, irregular spots on a green leaf seen in the test image.

Next, I'll view a reference image for Die_Back: `Prepared_Dataset/Mango_Leaf/Die_Back/leaf/Mango_Leaf_166.jpg`

The Die_Back reference image shows a completely dried, brown, and curled leaf. This is significantly different from the test image, which shows distinct spots on a still-green leaf.

Next, I'll view a reference image for Powdery_Mildew: `Prepared_Dataset/Mango_Leaf/Powdery_Mildew/leaf/Mango_Leaf_14.jpg`

Powdery_Mildew reference image shows a leaf covered in white, powdery patches. This is very different from the distinct dark spots in the test image.

Next, I'll view a reference image for Sooty_Mould: `Prepared_Dataset/Mango_Leaf/Sooty_Mould/leaf/Mango_Leaf_147.jpg`

The Sooty_Mould reference image shows dark, irregular, superficial patches on the leaf surface, which closely resembles the appearance of the test image. The "Sooty Mould" symptom description mentions "Dark sooty deposits on the upper surface of leaves and stems; the leaf remains green beneath the superficial mould layer; does not infect plant tissue but blocks sunlight from reaching leaf chloroplasts." This aligns well with the test image.

So far, Sooty_Mould is the closest visual match. I have used 4 out of 8 reference image views. I need to use all 8 views and spread them across at least 4 different classes. Since I've already viewed one from each of the 4 classes, I will revisit the classes that seem most plausible based on the initial visual comparison and symptom descriptions. Sooty_Mould looks like a strong candidate, and Anthracnose could also have dark spots. I will view more images from these two classes.

I will view another Anthracnose image: `Prepared_Dataset/Mango_Leaf/Anthracnose/leaf/Mango_Leaf_383.jpg`

This second Anthracnose image shows dark, irregular spots on a green leaf, which is much more similar to the test image than the first Anthracnose image I viewed. The symptom description for Anthracnose states: "Spots start small, black, and irregular on leaves, expanding into large dead areas that dry and fall out." This description also aligns with the test image.

Now I have two strong candidates: Sooty_Mould and Anthracnose. I will view another Sooty_Mould image to compare more closely. `Prepared_Dataset/Mango_Leaf/Sooty_Mould/leaf/Mango_Leaf_164.jpg`

thought
This second Sooty_Mould image also shows dark, somewhat diffuse patches on the leaf, similar to a superficial fungal growth. Comparing it to the second Anthracnose image and the test image, the spots in the test image and the second Anthracnose image appear more defined and potentially necrotic, whereas the Sooty_Mould appears more like a coating.

I have used 6 of 8 views. I need to use all 8 views and have spread them across at least 4 classes. I have viewed Anthracnose (2), Die_Back (1), Powdery_Mildew (1), Sooty_Mould (2). I will view two more images. I will view another Anthracnose image and another Sooty_Mould image to make a final decision, as these are the two strongest candidates.

I will view another Anthracnose image: `Prepared_Dataset/Mango_Leaf/Anthracnose/pod/Mango_Leaf_462.jpg` (although this is a pod, it's listed under Anthracnose and I need to use all views, and I'm already past the initial "spread across classes" rule).The second Sooty_Mould image shows dark, somewhat diffuse patches on the leaf, consistent with a superficial fungal growth. Comparing this to the second Anthracnose image and the test image, the spots in the test image and the second Anthracnose image appear more defined and potentially necrotic, while the Sooty_Mould appears more like a surface coating.

I have used 6 of 8 views. I will view another Anthracnose image and another Sooty_Mould image to solidify my decision.

I will view another Anthracnose image, even though it's a pod, as it's listed as a reference for Anthracnose and I need to use all 8 views: `Prepared_Dataset/Mango_Leaf/Anthracnose/pod/Mango_Leaf_462.jpg`

This Anthracnose reference image of a pod shows significant browning and drying, with irregular lesions. While it shows damage, it's on a different plant part and doesn't directly help in distinguishing between the leaf spots in the test image and Sooty Mould.

I have used 7 of 8 views. I will view one more Sooty_Mould image: `Prepared_Dataset/Mango_Leaf/Sooty_Mould/leaf/Mango_Leaf_288.jpg`
